page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an ARM64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under the QEMU hypervisor. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this server type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate CPU capabilities alongside constrained memory and specialized processing performance. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests yield average results of 1805.19 and 7235.85, respectively. However, memory bandwidth is weak, with read-only large block speeds at 38.95 GB/sec and write speeds at 25.37 GB/sec. Passmark database operations perform at an average level of 2796.83, while cryptographic and image processing tasks show poor performance, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 646.59 and a Geekbench image processing score of 1882.0.

Given its shared ARM64 architecture and lower memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2, the cax21 offers a resource-dense, entry-level hardware profile. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or high memory bandwidth. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight database operations, simple text processing, and development or testing environments that can leverage the ARM64 instruction set without demanding high-performance vector or cryptographic extensions.
